facts.statement: The only known fossil of Lavocatavis is a single femur described from the Glib Zegdou Formation in 2011.
facts.quote: A fossilized femur was described from the Glib Zegdou Formation in 2011 and is the only known specimen of Lavocatavis.

facts.statement: The genus name Lavocatavis means "Lavocat's bird" and honors René Lavocat, who first reported the geological layer containing the fossil.
facts.quote: The generic epithet (meaning "Lavocat's bird") was named in honor of René Lavocat, the person who first reported the earth layer of the holotype.

facts.statement: Lavocatavis lived during the Eocene epoch in Algeria.
facts.quote: Lavocatavis is an extinct genus of prehistoric bird from the Eocene of Algeria.

facts.statement: Lavocatavis lived between 56 and 41.03 million years ago during the Ypresian to Lutetian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Lutetian (56 to 41.03 million years ago)

facts.statement: Lavocatavis has been tentatively classified as a member of the family Phorusrhacidae, but this placement is considered highly questionable due to fragmentary remains.
facts.quote: Along with Eleutherornis, it has been considered as a possible member of the family Phorusrhacidae outside the Americas, but the taxonomic identity of both taxa is considered highly questionable.

facts.statement: Because the Atlantic Ocean separated South America from Africa during the Eocene, researchers suggest Lavocatavis ancestors likely arrived in Africa via rafting on floating islands or island hopping.
facts.quote: For a flightless terrestrial bird like Lavocatavis, the only means of entering Africa would have been through rafting on floating islands or island hopping.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Lavocatavis ancestors retained some flight ability, which would have allowed them to travel between islands more easily than flightless birds.
facts.quote: However, it is also possible that the ancestors of Lavocatavis retained some of their flight ability and were able to travel between islands with more ease than flightless birds.

facts.statement: The single known femur of Lavocatavis is nearly as large as that of Patagornis.
facts.quote: Un fémur fosilizado, casi tan grande como el de Patagornis fue descrito en la formación Glib Zegdou en 2011 y es el único espécimen conocido de Lavocatavis.

rejected.statement: Researcher Gerald Mayr suggested that Lavocatavis is likely more closely related to the paleognath Eremopezus than to other phorusrhacids.
rejected.quote: Gerald Mayr suggested that ... Lavocatavis is likely more related to a possible paleognath Eremopezus, questioning the taxonomic placement of both taxa as phorusrhacids.
